author: big sky times
title: Researcher on Indigenous bison stewardship receives Montana State's 2026 Distinctive Collections Travel and Access Award
text:
A researcher studying Indigenous bison stewardship has been awarded the Montana State University Library’s Distinctive Collections Travel and Access Award, according to a May 20 announcement. Josias Agustin Mendez, a Ph.D. candidate at Columbia University, received the $3,000 honorarium to support his research in Bozeman.
The award aims to help scholars access unique materials at MSU Archives and Special Collections. Mendez will use the funding for summer travel as he works on his dissertation chapter analyzing how members of the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes responded to the creation of the National Bison Range in 1908 on reservation land.
This is the sixth time that MSU has given this award. It is a collaborative effort between the Ivan Doig Center for the Study of the Lands and Peoples of the North American West, MSU Archives and Special Collections, and Friends of MSU Library. Funding comes from both Friends of MSU Library and the Doig Center.
The university offers research resources not only to its students but also to citizens across Montana. Its archives include manuscripts focused on agricultural history, trout and salmonids, regional books, angling collections, select records from MSU itself, among other topics. For more information about these collections or about Ivan Doig Center programs fostering study across disciplines related to the American West, readers can visit www.lib.montana.edu/archives/ or www.montana.edu/doig/.
Friends of Montana State University Library was founded in 1994 with a mission to develop library collections, spaces, programs and community presence. More details are available at www.lib.montana.edu/about/friends.
Montana State University leads in research funding within Montana with annual expenditures exceeding $288 million; it enrolls approximately 17,165 students split evenly between residents and nonresidents; it ranks among top global universities per international rankings; contributes through outreach efforts aimed at enhancing lives statewide; operates as Montana’s land-grant institution focusing on education and community needs; extends its influence beyond state borders—all according to the official website.
